executiveSummary: Manifest audits every freight invoice before it is paid. Mid-market shippers lose 4% of freight spend to billing errors that today's audit firms find months late and charge a third to recover. Our 38 paid pilots recovered 4.2% of spend and ARR grew fivefold this year to $910K. We are raising a $4M seed to reach 120 shippers and $5M ARR.

slides.slideTitle: Manifest stops shippers paying for freight they never shipped
slides.subtitle: Seed round · $4M · Automated freight invoice audit for mid-market shippers
slides.visualDescription: A loading dock at dawn, trucks backed into bays, a single invoice glowing on a tablet in the foreground
slides.speakerNotes:
- Thanks for the time. We're Manifest, and we audit every freight invoice before it gets paid.
- We're raising a $4M seed to take what worked in our pilots to the mid-market.
- Fifteen minutes: the problem, what it costs, why today's fixes fail, and what we built.
slides.purpose: Names the company and the promise in one line
slides.intent: Make them curious why freight invoices need auditing

slides.slideTitle: One in twelve freight invoices is wrong, and nobody checks
slides.subtitle: Mid-market shippers pay carriers on trust because auditing by hand doesn't scale
slides.visualDescription: A stack of thousands of invoices on a desk, one highlighted in red, the rest blurring into shadow
slides.speakerNotes:
- Here's the uncomfortable truth we found in every pilot.
- About 8% of freight invoices carry an error, almost always in the carrier's favor.
- A shipper moving 20,000 loads a year can't read every line, so they don't.
- They pay what they're billed and hope the carrier got it right.
slides.purpose: States the core problem as a single hard fact
slides.intent: Make them feel the scale of unchecked overbilling

slides.slideTitle: Billing errors drain $9 billion from US shippers every year
slides.subtitle: Duplicate charges, wrong accessorials, and rate drift add up
keyBullets: Lost each year by US shippers to freight invoice errors
slides.visualDescription: A single enormous dollar figure over a highway at night, trucks streaking past as light trails
slides.speakerNotes:
- We took the error rate from 2.1 million invoices we audited and applied it to US freight spend.
- That's $9 billion a year, paid and never recovered.
- For a typical mid-market shipper, that's $400K to $1.2M walking out the door.
- And nobody on their team owns finding it.
slides.purpose: Quantifies the cost of inaction with a single dollar figure
slides.intent: Make them feel that ignoring this is itself expensive
slides.supportingFacts: Manifest analysis of 2.1M invoices from 38 pilot shippers, applied to $1.1T US freight spend

slides.slideTitle: Accessorial charges cause most of the overbilling we found
slides.subtitle: Share of overbilled dollars by error type, 38 pilot shippers
keyBullets: Accessorials alone are 41% of every overbilled dollar
slides.speakerNotes:
- Accessorials are the extras: liftgates, detention, residential delivery.
- They're billed after the fact and rarely match the contract.
- Duplicates are next: the same load billed twice through two channels.
- Rate drift is the quiet one: last year's rate, this year's invoice.
slides.purpose: Shows where the money leaks so the problem feels concrete
slides.intent: Make them believe the errors are systematic, not random

slides.slideTitle: We knew we were overpaying but couldn't afford to find out
keyBullets: We knew we were overpaying. We just couldn't afford to find out by how much.
Dana Whitfield, VP Logistics, Corvane Foods
slides.visualDescription: Portrait of a logistics manager in a warehouse office, invoices pinned to a corkboard behind her
slides.speakerNotes: Dana runs logistics for a $600M food distributor. Before Manifest, her team of four sampled two hundred invoices a month out of nine thousand. She knew the money was there; she had no way to get it without hiring an audit firm that would take a third of it.
slides.purpose: Gives the problem a human voice from a real buyer
slides.intent: Make them feel the buyer's frustration with the status quo

slides.slideTitle: Audit every invoice before it is paid
slides.subtitle: Introducing Manifest
slides.visualDescription: A single invoice on a dark background, a green check mark drawing itself across it
slides.speakerNotes:
- So we built the audit that happens before the money moves.
- Let me show you how it works.
slides.purpose: Turns the deck from problem to solution
slides.intent: Signal that the answer is coming

slides.slideTitle: Manifest checks each invoice against the contract in seconds
keyBullets: Read: invoices arrive by EDI, email, or carrier portal and are parsed line by line
Match: each charge is checked against the shipment, the contract rate, and proof of delivery
Dispute: anything that doesn't match is disputed with the carrier before AP pays
slides.visualDescription: A clean three-panel diagram: an invoice, a contract, and a dispute email connected by glowing lines
slides.speakerNotes:
- Three steps, all automatic.
- We read every invoice format carriers send, including scanned PDFs.
- We match each charge to the contract and to what actually happened on the dock.
- When something's wrong, we file the dispute with evidence attached.
- AP only ever sees verified amounts.
slides.purpose: Explains the mechanism so the claim feels credible
slides.intent: Make them believe the product is real and simple to adopt

slides.slideTitle: Audit moves from months after payment to seconds before it
keyBullets: Before: 60 days to find an error, and a 30% fee to recover it
After: errors caught in 4 seconds and disputed before payment
slides.speakerNotes:
- This is the shift that matters.
- Recovery after payment is slow, adversarial, and expensive.
- Prevention before payment is fast and the carrier usually just reissues the invoice.
- Our pilots disputed before payment 94% of the time.
slides.purpose: Shows the transformation in one comparison
slides.intent: Make them feel how much better prevention is than recovery

slides.slideTitle: Pilots recovered 4.2% of freight spend within 90 days
slides.subtitle: Results from 38 paid pilots, January–September 2026
keyBullets: 4.2%: of freight spend recovered
38: shippers in paid pilots
2.1M: invoices audited
97%: of disputes won
slides.speakerNotes:
- These are paid pilots, not free trials.
- 4.2% of spend recovered is real money: $840K for a shipper spending $20M.
- We've audited 2.1 million invoices, so the error rates aren't a fluke.
- Carriers accept 97% of our disputes because we attach the evidence.
slides.purpose: Proves the product works with hard numbers
slides.intent: Make them believe the results are repeatable

slides.slideTitle: ARR grew fivefold this year to $910K
slides.subtitle: Annual recurring revenue by month, 2026, $K
keyBullets: ARR reached $910K in September, up 5× since January
slides.speakerNotes:
- We converted 31 of 38 pilots to annual contracts.
- Growth has come entirely from referrals and two logistics conferences.
- No paid acquisition yet; that's part of what this round funds.
- Net revenue retention is 138% because customers add carriers and sites.
slides.intent: Make them feel momentum they want to be part of

slides.slideTitle: A $2.4B market sits inside mid-market freight spend
slides.subtitle: From all US freight to the shippers we can reach today
keyBullets: US freight spend: $1.1T a year
Mid-market shippers: $180B of it, 14,000 companies
On EDI with top carriers: $60B, 4,200 companies
Our audit fee: $2.4B a year at 4% of recovered value
slides.speakerNotes:
- We start with mid-market shippers, $10M to $200M in freight spend.
- They're too small for the big audit firms and too big to check by hand.
- 4,200 of them already exchange EDI with the top carriers, so onboarding is days, not months.
- That's a $2.4B revenue opportunity before we touch enterprise.
slides.intent: Make them believe the market can support a large company
